title: Long-Channel MOSFET I-V Explorer
description: Output characteristics (drain current against drain voltage for a family of gate voltages) and the logarithmic transfer curve of a long-channel MOSFET from the square-law model with channel-length modulation and subthreshold conduction. The triode, saturation, and cutoff regions are marked, a sketch shows the channel charge and pinch-off, and a readout gives the transconductance, output conductance, intrinsic gain, and subthreshold slope at the operating point.
creator: Dan McCreary

chapter_title: JFET, MESFET, and Long-Channel MOSFET Fundamentals

educational.topic: Current-voltage characteristics of the long-channel MOSFET
learningObjectives: Identify the triode, saturation, and cutoff regions on the output characteristics
Calculate the transconductance and output conductance from the current-voltage data
Explain what the subthreshold slope means and why about 60 mV per decade is its lower limit at room temperature
Compare the predictions of the long-channel model with the behavior expected of a short-channel transistor
prerequisites: The MOS capacitor and threshold voltage
MOSFET structure and the gradual channel approximation

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders with two linked real-time plots, a channel sketch, and a small-signal readout at the operating point
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe, followed by hand calculation of small-signal parameters checked against the readout
assessmentOpportunities: Find the drain voltage at which the transistor leaves saturation
Compute the transconductance and output conductance by hand
Measure the subthreshold slope from two points on the logarithmic plot

controls.label: Gate voltage V_GS
controls.purpose: Gate voltage of the operating point

controls.label: Drain voltage V_DS
controls.purpose: Drain voltage of the operating point

equations: Triode: I_D = (k/2)[2(V_GS - V_T)V_DS - V_DS^2](1 + lambda V_DS), k = mu C_ox W/L
Saturation: I_D = (k/2)(V_GS - V_T)^2 (1 + lambda V_DS), V_DS,sat = V_GS - V_T
Subthreshold: I_D proportional to exp((V_GS - V_T)/(n V_th)), S = n V_th ln(10)
Smooth interpolation: I_D = (k/2)(v_f^2 - v_r^2)(1 + lambda V_DS), v = 2 n V_th ln(1 + exp(x / 2 n V_th))
assumptions: Gradual channel approximation, source and body at the same potential
Channel-length modulation factor applied in triode and saturation for continuity
limitations: No velocity saturation, drain-induced barrier lowering, mobility degradation, or body effect
Slightly above the square law within about 0.2 V of threshold
The channel sketch is not to scale
